To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Mgat3 expression and GnTIII-mediated glycosylations on E-cad-herin are key components of the EMT and MET mechanism signature, supporting the role of GnTIII-mediated N-glycosylations during these transitions.
GnT-III is involved in EMT/MET through its effect on E-cad expression and that this is mediated by Mgat3 expression.
the expression and activity of Mgat3, a glycosylating enzyme, is regulated during EMT/MEM, leading to the specific glycosylation of E-cad, and this glycosylation has a role in EMT/MET regulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms that control the glycosylation of E-cad herin, a major regulator of cell-cell interactions.
the molecular mechanisms involved in the EMT and the reverted process MET.
the molecular mechanism involved in the regulation of Mgat3 gene expression, and the role of GnT- III-mediated glycosylation in EMT/MET.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Mgat3 and the enzymatic product GnT-III, are key regulators during EMT/Met, and that GnT-III mediated E-cadherins glycosylation with β1,4-GlcNAc is an important molecular mechanism during the process of EMT/MET.
GnT-III is a metastases suppressors, but the Mgat3/GnT-III-mediated bisecting Glcnac structures are a metastasis enhancer.

the loss and recovery of Mgat3-mediated glycosylation is a mechanism involved in EMT/MET and the variation in E-cadherins N-glycosylations is a mechanism involved on E-cad herin expression regulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Mgat3 expression and GnTIII-mediated E-cadherine N-glycosylaiton, is a novel mechanism involved in EMT/MET.
the loss and recovery of GnT- III-mediated E-cadherins N-glycosylations, during EMT and MET, respectively, is a major molecular mechanism involved in these transitions.
Mgat3 and its enzymatic product GnT-III, specifically on E-Cadherin, are a mechanism involved in EMT/MET.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the expression of GnT-3 and the presence of bisecting Glcnac on E-cad are a major determinant of epithelial phenotype and that the loss of GnT- III and bisecting Glnc is a major component of the epithelial-mesenchymal transition.
GnT-III and Mgat3 are key regulators of EMT/MET and therefore, they could be used as potential biomarkers and/or targets for the treatment of metastatic cancer.
Mgat3 expression and GnTIII-mediated glycosylations are involved in EMT/MET regulation.
